entities.name: HIV-1 Tat
observations: The 100-aa query sequence matches reviewed HIV-1 Tat proteins with 72.0–77.3% identity, 97–100% query coverage, and E-values of 1.9e-47 to 3.4e-50.
Pfam scanning identifies the Tat domain PF00539.24 at positions 2–63 with i-Evalue 1.1e-33.
Tat is an RNA-binding transcriptional activator that binds the HIV TAR RNA element and recruits P-TEFb, increasing RNA polymerase II transcription elongation.
Tat is reported in the host nucleus, nucleolus, cytoplasm, and extracellular space; nuclear/nucleolar localization is supported by a Lys/Arg-rich nuclear localization region.

Associated biological processes include positive regulation of viral transcription, positive regulation of RNA polymerase II elongation, proviral chromatin remodeling, and suppression of host innate immune responses.

Sequence-derived properties for the query: 100 aa, approximately 11.46 kDa, predicted pI 9.95, charge at pH 7 approximately +13.9, consistent with a highly basic nucleic-acid/protein-interaction factor.

The cysteine-rich region is compatible with Tat's metal-ion-binding/transactivation domain, but exact metal coordination and effects of post-translational modifications are not established from sequence alone.
